content.value_statement: Raw data is hard to interpret without the right chart. This skill helps create clear static and interactive visualizations with practical library examples.
actual_capabilities: Maps common analysis goals to chart types and use cases.
Provides Matplotlib examples for bar, line, pie, scatter, histogram, box, and heatmap charts.
Provides Seaborn examples for grouped, faceted, distribution, violin, pairplot, and heatmap charts.
Provides Plotly examples for interactive bars, lines, scatter plots, 3D scatter plots, time series, and dashboards.
Provides Chart.js examples for server-rendered bar, line, and pie charts.
Describes themes, color palettes, multi-format exports, and batch chart generation.
limitations: The skill contains reusable examples, not a packaged command-line application.
Users must provide clean data and confirm column names before generating charts.
Generated examples may need dependency installation for Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, Chart.js, or chartjs-node-canvas.
It does not validate privacy risks in source datasets.

use_cases.title: Prepare Business Charts
use_cases.description: Turn sales, finance, or product data into comparison, trend, and composition charts for reports.

use_cases.title: Explore Data Relationships
use_cases.description: Select scatter plots, heatmaps, histograms, and box plots to understand distributions and correlations.

use_cases.title: Build Interactive Reporting Views
use_cases.description: Plan Plotly or Chart.js charts for dashboards, hover details, time series controls, and HTML exports.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one chart from a known dataset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use chart-generator to recommend a chart for this dataset: [describe columns]. Explain the chart choice and export format.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Report Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a presentation-ready visualization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use chart-generator to create a polished figure plan for [business question]. Include chart type, axes, title, labels, and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Interactive Dashboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple connected visualizations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use chart-generator to design an interactive Plotly dashboard for [dataset]. Include the chart layout, filters, hover behavior, and export approach.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Visualization Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing chart workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use chart-generator to review this chart workflow: [workflow]. Improve chart selection, file outputs, themes, and reusable generation steps.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks for a monthly revenue trend by region.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a multi-series line chart with date on the x-axis, revenue on the y-axis, region as color, and an HTML export for hover details.

output_examples.input: A data analyst needs a correlation view for numeric feature columns.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a heatmap with a diverging color scale, visible correlation labels, readable axis rotation, and a high-resolution image export.

output_examples.input: A developer wants three chart formats from the same dataset.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a batch generation approach that creates PNG, SVG, and PDF files with consistent titles, labels, and color palettes.

best_practices: Start with the decision the chart must support, then choose the simplest chart type.
Label axes, units, legends, and annotations so viewers can read the chart without extra context.
Use accessible color palettes and test the chart with realistic data ranges.
anti_patterns: Do not use pie charts for many categories or precise comparisons.
Do not export charts before validating column names, missing values, and units.
Do not add decorative effects that reduce readability or accessibility.

faq.question: Does this skill run chart code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example patterns that the host agent can adapt in the active workspace.

faq.question: Which chart libraries are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, and Chart.js examples.

faq.question: Can it create interactive charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Plotly examples for interactive HTML charts, time series controls, 3D scatter plots, and dashboards.

faq.question: Does it support exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes PNG, SVG, PDF, JPG, and HTML chart outputs.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide column names, sample rows, chart goal, audience, and preferred output format.

faq.question: Can it choose the best chart type?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance that maps common analysis goals to chart types.
